title: Data & Document Handling | How JPNentry treats business information
description: How JPNentry handles RFQs, specifications, quotes, screenshots, supplier information and other business documents.
content:
JPNentry handles commercial information on a need-to-know basis for the purpose of evaluating, verifying or executing the requested service.
Typical information we may receive
• RFQ sheets, part numbers, quantities and target prices
• Product specifications, photos, model / chassis information
• Travel group requirements, dates, participant information and service preferences
• Quotations, supplier replies, freight indications and commercial terms
• Screenshots or files submitted to verify a JPNentry message or payment request
How the information is used
We use submitted information to evaluate the relevant request, communicate with potential suppliers or partners when necessary, prepare recommendations / quotations, verify commercial conditions and manage the associated project record.
Data minimization
We prefer the minimum information necessary to perform the requested work. Sensitive personal information that is not needed for a sourcing, travel or verification task should not be sent.
Third-party sharing
Where a live project requires supplier, operator, logistics or other third-party checks, the relevant commercial or technical details may need to be shared with those parties. We aim to limit that sharing to what is necessary for the check or transaction.
Passwords and authentication
JPNentry does not ask customers to send passwords, one-time authentication codes or remote-access credentials.
Payment-card data
For published card-payment services, payment collection is handled through Stripe-hosted payment pages. JPNentry does not ask customers to email card numbers or security codes.
Verification submissions
Files and screenshots submitted through the Trust & Verification Request are used to determine whether the referenced communication, quote, invoice, supplier claim or payment request is genuine and to respond to the requester.
Need clarification?
If you need a data-handling condition to be confirmed in writing for a specific project, ask before sending commercially sensitive material.

title: JPNentry FAQ | Buyers, suppliers and partners
description: Answers to common questions about JPNentry sourcing, verification, payments, AI Visibility Audit and business communication.
content:
This FAQ is designed for buyers, suppliers and partners who want to understand how JPNentry works before starting a transaction.
Is JPNentry a marketplace?
No. JPNentry is a Japan-side sourcing, verification, market-entry and coordination service. We do not claim to own all quoted inventory or operate as a general online marketplace.
Do you guarantee stock?
No. Stock is only treated as confirmed when the relevant supplier or source has confirmed the applicable item, quantity and timing. Public listings are not treated as confirmed stock.
Can you source genuine/OEM only?
Yes, when the buyer specifies genuine/OEM only. We do not silently substitute aftermarket, used, refreshed or alternative products without explicit approval.
Do you guarantee the lowest price?
No. We compare commercial viability, but we do not claim every Japan source will be the cheapest. If Japan is not competitive for a requirement, we may return a no-go.
Why would a buyer pay for Priority RFQ Verification?
Because difficult requirements can consume significant Japan-side verification time. The paid service is for buyers who want a structured answer on one live requirement rather than a large list of unverified supplier links.
Does the AI Visibility Audit guarantee ChatGPT or Gemini ranking?
No. It is a diagnostic service. We examine public information, consistency, discoverability signals and representative AI-assisted search questions. We do not control or guarantee any AI platform's output.
Can I verify an email, quote or payment request?
Yes. Use the Trust & Verification Request before sending money or sensitive information if anything is unclear.
Can I opt out of outreach?
Yes. Use the Contact Preferences page. We treat opt-out and duplicate-outreach reports seriously.
Do you require a meeting?
Not for the published one-time diagnostic services. Many workflows can be completed through forms and email. Meetings are used only when they materially help a live project.

title: AI Visibility Audit Methodology | What JPNentry actually checks
description: A transparent explanation of the JPNentry AI Visibility Audit methodology, scope and limitations.
content:
JPNentry AI Visibility Audit is a diagnostic service for businesses that want to understand how their public information may be interpreted in AI-assisted discovery.
What we review
• Public-facing website information and key service/product descriptions
• Consistency of business facts across visible public sources where relevant
• Whether important differentiators, audiences, languages, locations and service conditions are easy to understand
• Representative questions a prospective customer may ask ChatGPT, Gemini or other AI-assisted search experiences
• Information gaps, ambiguity, contradictory signals and weak comparison criteria
• Priority improvements and a practical action roadmap
What a score means
Any score or assessment in the report is an internal diagnostic framework designed to prioritize improvements. It is not an official score from OpenAI, Google, Microsoft or any search platform.
What we do not promise
We do not guarantee that a specific AI system will mention, rank or recommend a business. AI outputs can vary by model, time, user context, language and source availability.
Why the audit can still be useful
The practical objective is to improve clarity, consistency and evidence in public information so customers—and AI systems that rely on public information—have better material to understand the business.
Independence
JPNentry is not claiming affiliation with OpenAI, Google, Microsoft or the AI/search providers referenced in diagnostic examples.

title: JPNentry Commercial & Payment Policy | What is included and what is not
description: How JPNentry handles service fees, payment requests, sourcing transactions and commercial limitations.
content:
This policy is intended to make commercial expectations clear before money changes hands.
Service fees
Published one-time services such as AI Visibility Audit and Priority RFQ Verification are charged at the price shown on the official JPNentry service page and Stripe payment page at the time of purchase.
Work starts after the required intake information and the service payment are both confirmed.
Goods and sourcing transactions
A sourcing-verification service fee does not include the cost of goods, freight, insurance, customs duties, import taxes, third-party inspection fees or supplier charges unless explicitly stated in a written quotation.
For goods transactions, the purchase/payment structure is agreed after the item, source, specification, quantity, price and commercial basis have been confirmed.
No hidden substitution
If a buyer requests genuine/OEM only, we do not replace it with aftermarket, refreshed or used product without explicit approval.
No artificial guarantees
We do not guarantee supplier stock, manufacturer pricing, export approval, freight capacity, customs clearance, AI ranking, leads, bookings or sales unless a specific contractual guarantee is explicitly written.
Changes and validity
Supplier stock, exchange rates, manufacturer pricing, freight rates and availability can change. Quotations may therefore have a stated validity period or require reconfirmation before order placement.
Refund / cancellation basis
For diagnostic or verification services, once substantive work has started, the fee covers the research/verification work and not a guaranteed commercial outcome. If JPNentry has not started the paid service, a cancellation request can be reviewed before work begins.
Disputes and verification
If you are uncertain whether a payment request, invoice or email is genuine, do not pay first. Use the Trust & Verification Request form and ask us to verify it.

title: Japan Sourcing Verification Standard | How JPNentry checks a live RFQ
description: The verification rules JPNentry follows before presenting Japan-side sourcing information to an overseas buyer.
content:
JPNentry is enquiry-driven. We do not present a generic supplier directory as if it were confirmed stock.
1. Exact requirement first
We begin from an exact part number, SKU, model, specification, quantity, condition requirement, destination and timing whenever available.
2. Sourceability is separated from availability
A part being listed online does not mean it is available in the requested quantity. We distinguish between visible listings, supplier-confirmed stock, manufacturer/orderable quantity and estimated future supply.
3. Specification is checked before substitution
Genuine/OEM, aftermarket, refreshed and used are treated as different commercial categories. We do not silently substitute one for another.
4. Price basis is stated
Where possible, quotations identify whether pricing is Japan-side goods value, Ex-Warehouse / FCA / FOB / CIF or another basis. Freight, duties and third-party charges are separated unless explicitly included.
5. Lead time is not invented
Lead time is presented as supplier-confirmed or estimated. If a manufacturer price or stock level must be reconfirmed at order time, that condition is disclosed.
6. Export feasibility is a separate check
Dangerous goods, batteries, restricted items, oversized cargo and regulated products require a separate transport/export feasibility check. Product availability alone does not mean export is possible.
7. Red flags are disclosed
Where a source, price, quantity, stock claim or commercial condition appears inconsistent, we flag it instead of presenting it as verified.
8. Clear no-go is an acceptable result
If Japan is not commercially realistic for the requirement, JPNentry may return a no-go instead of forcing an unsuitable quote.
9. Final transaction terms are written
Before a purchase commitment, the commercial basis should identify item/specification, quantity, unit price, currency, payment terms, lead time, validity, delivery basis and material limitations.
